command_template: python3 tools/debian_native_container_probe.py CLIENT NEW_DEB NEW_SHA256 NEW_SKILL_ZIP SKILL_SHA256 --old-package OLD_DEB --old-sha256 OLD_SHA256 --fixture-mode dns-rebind --container-memory-mib 128 --sample-server-resources
limitations: The old package ran a direct MCP initialize and loopback-denial smoke before upgrade; it was not called by a native client before upgrade in this run.

Versions 205 and 214 are unsigned experimental packages, not successive official release candidates. Local artifact checksums were verified; local replay did not independently verify provenance signatures.

The DNS fixture observes two A lookups and three allowed HTTP hits; it does not provide packet-wide proof of no forbidden connection or cover other resolver implementations, networks or all rebinding timings.

Configuration migration, other supported platforms, Cursor, automatic triggering, UI cancellation and traffic through other tools remain outside this replay. Independent human review was not obtained (optional for Outbound Guard).

container_resource_observation.scope: Container cgroup high-water marks include setup and helper processes; not server-only RSS or FD peaks.

server_resource_observation.scope: Finite sampled server observations; sampling can miss transient peaks.

old_package_preupgrade_mcp_smoke: Inside each upgrade container, before dpkg upgraded the package, check installed version and executable SHA-256, launch the old executable, negotiate MCP initialize, and assert guarded_fetch denied a loopback URL with EGRESS_INVALID_HOST. After upgrade check new version/executable SHA-256 and make five native-client guarded calls.
tested_boundary: After package upgrade, explicit native skill calls to a route-free controlled DNS/HTTP fixture. The first rebind.test lookup returns a public-policy fixture address; the second returns loopback. The fixture counts two A lookups and exactly three approved HTTP hits. This finite observation does not capture every host packet.
